user.title: Connect ProgressCove
user.description: Create an API token in the ProgressCove app under Settings → Advanced → API tokens, then paste it here.

data_description.url: Leave as-is for ProgressCove's own servers, or enter your address if you self-host.
data_description.token: Starts with pat_. It is shown once, when you create it.

lists.title: Choose your lists
lists.description: Any node can be a list. Its direct children become the items. The ones already holding items are ticked for you. Add a task you are about to break into subtasks, or untick a branch you do not want. Each list gets its own row on the integration page. Change them later with "Manage lists" there.

data_description.lists: Each one becomes a to-do list. Its direct children become the items.

reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect ProgressCove
reauth_confirm.description: Your API token is no longer valid. Create a new one and paste it here.

reconfigure.title: Change the server or token
reconfigure.description: Where this Home Assistant reaches ProgressCove, and optionally a replacement token. Leave the token empty to keep the current one. A new token is paired the same way the first one was.

pair.title: Pair with ProgressCove
pair.description:
Open ProgressCove, go to Settings → Advanced → API tokens, and pair this token using the code:

**{code}**

Then continue.

insecure.title: This address is not encrypted
insecure.description:
{url} uses http, so your token and your task names travel across the network in the open. That is fine on a network you trust and control. It is not fine over the internet, where anyone between you and the server can read them.

Continue only if you know this address stays on your own network.

reconfigure_insecure.title: This address is not encrypted
reconfigure_insecure.description:
{url} uses http, so your token and your task names travel across the network in the open. That is fine on a network you trust and control. It is not fine over the internet, where anyone between you and the server can read them.

Continue only if you know this address stays on your own network.

read_only.title: This token is read-only
read_only.description:
Your lists and cards will show your tasks, but ticking, adding and buttons are off. To turn them on, create a read and write token in ProgressCove and paste it under Reconfigure on the integration page.

Continue to set up with what this token can do.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the server. Check the address and try again.
error.invalid_auth: That token was not accepted. It may have been revoked.
error.no_projects: That account has no projects yet. Create one in the app first.
error.not_paired_yet: Not paired yet. Enter the code in ProgressCove, then try again.
error.invalid_url: That does not look like a web address. It should start with https://
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. Try again, and if it keeps happening, check the Home Assistant log.
error.not_selectable: One of those rows cannot be a list. Pick another.
error.subscription_inactive: This account's ProgressCove subscription is not active. Renew it in the app under Settings → Sunrise, then try again.

abort.already_configured: This account is already set up.
abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach the server. Check the address and try again.
abort.already_in_progress: This account is already being set up.
abort.wrong_account: That token belongs to a different ProgressCove account. To switch accounts, remove the integration and add it again.

init.title: ProgressCove settings
init.description: Choosing your lists is the "Manage lists" button at the top of this page. These are the settings behind it.

data.auto_prune: Remove entities when their task is deleted
data.complete_early: Allow completing before the due date

data_description.min_depth: The highest level a list can come from.
data_description.max_depth: The deepest. Set both the same to pick from just that one.
data_description.node_sort: Task name first is easier to type; full path is easier to browse by project.
data_description.auto_prune: Off: once the server confirms a task is gone, Repairs offers to remove its list, button, switch or sensor in one step. On: they are removed without asking, once the server confirms it.
data_description.complete_early: Off: a task that is not due yet is refused, because completing a repeat early moves it past the occurrence you were waiting for. On: complete anything whenever you like.

user.title: Manage lists
user.description: Any node can be a list. Its direct children become the items. Rows marked with a dash are context only. Ticked rows are your lists now: tick a row to add it, untick one to remove it.

error.not_selectable: One of those rows is context only. Pick a row without a dash.

user.title: Add a list
user.description: Pick any node. Its direct children become the list's items. To add or remove several lists at once, use "Manage lists".

abort.no_tasks_left: Everything on offer is already a list.

error.unavailable: That one can no longer be picked. Choose another.

user.title: Add a button
user.description: Pick any item. Pressing the button completes today's occurrence of it.

abort.no_tasks_left: Every task already has a button.
abort.already_configured: That task already has a button.

error.unavailable: That one can no longer be picked. Choose another.

user.title: Add a switch
user.description: Pick any item. The switch is on while it is open; turning it off completes it. A repeating task waits ten seconds before it is sent, so turning it back on inside that window undoes it. Anything else reopens normally whenever you like.

abort.no_tasks_left: Every task already has a switch.
abort.already_configured: That task already has a switch.

error.unavailable: That one can no longer be picked. Choose another.

user.title: Add a progress sensor
user.description: Pick any item that has things under it. The sensor reports how far through them it is, as a percentage you can graph. For "when this is finished", trigger on the list's own items_complete attribute instead. It is a plain true/false.

abort.already_configured: That already has a progress sensor.

error.unavailable: That one can no longer be picked. Choose another.

stale_entities.title: Some entities point at deleted tasks

confirm.title: Remove entities for deleted tasks
confirm.description:
ProgressCove confirmed these tasks no longer exist: {names}.

Removing their entities also removes them from any automation or dashboard that uses them.

error.cannot_connect: Could not check with ProgressCove, so nothing was removed. Try again in a moment.

abort.cannot_connect: Could not check with ProgressCove, so nothing was removed. Try again in a moment.
abort.nothing_to_remove: Those tasks are back in ProgressCove, so their entities stay.
abort.not_loaded: ProgressCove is not running right now. Reload the integration and try again.

unconfirmed_entities.title: Some entities point at tasks that could not be checked
unconfirmed_entities.description: These could not be confirmed with the server, so nothing was removed: {names}. If you deleted those tasks, delete these from the integration page. If not, they will come back on their own once the server is reachable.

read_only.title: ProgressCove is read-only
read_only.description: The token this Home Assistant uses can only read. Lists and cards show your tasks, but ticking, adding and buttons are off. To turn them on, create a read and write token in ProgressCove under Settings → Advanced → API tokens, then open this integration, choose Reconfigure from its menu and paste the new token there.

inbox_unavailable.title: ProgressCove's inbox could not be loaded
inbox_unavailable.description:
Home Assistant could not load your ProgressCove inbox, so the Inbox list is missing. The server answered: {reason}

Once the cause is fixed, reload this integration from its menu to try again.

subscription_inactive.title: ProgressCove subscription is not active
subscription_inactive.description:
ProgressCove refused to send your tasks because this account's subscription is not active, so everything it shows here is unavailable. Renew it in the ProgressCove app under Settings → Sunrise.

There is nothing to do here afterwards: Home Assistant keeps checking every few minutes, reconnects by itself once the subscription is active, and this message goes away. If your subscription is already active, ProgressCove could not confirm it just now, and this clears up on its own.

read_only.message: This ProgressCove token is read-only, so nothing was changed. Create a read and write token and paste it under Reconfigure on the integration page.

rejected.message: ProgressCove did not accept that change: {reason}

complete_failed.message: ProgressCove could not complete that task.

reopen_failed.message: ProgressCove could not reopen that task.

add_failed.message: ProgressCove could not add that task.

update_failed.message: ProgressCove could not update that task.

delete_failed.message: ProgressCove could not delete that task.

not_due_yet.message: {name} is not due yet, next on {due}.

repeat_cannot_reopen.message: {name} repeats, so completing it moved it to its next occurrence. Reopening it here would leave it on the wrong day. Change it in the ProgressCove app.

unknown_node.message: No ProgressCove task with id {node_id}. Copy it from a card or the node_id attribute.

not_loaded.message: No ProgressCove account is loaded right now. The integration page says why.

complete_not_sent.message: Completing "{name}" did not go through. It was not saved and the task is unchanged.

subscription_inactive.message: ProgressCove refused this because the account's subscription is not active. Renew it in the app under Settings → Sunrise.

not_my_day.message: {entity_id} is not a ProgressCove My Day list. This action only answers for My Day.

complete.name: Complete a task
complete.description: Mark any ProgressCove task done, at any depth, including a subtask that is not one of a list's own items and so cannot be reached with todo.update_item. A repeating task is held for ten seconds before it is sent, so calling reopen inside that window cancels it; anything else is sent straight away and reopens normally.

node_id.name: Task
node_id.description: The task's id. Read it from a card, or from the node_id attribute of its button or switch.

reopen.name: Reopen a task
reopen.description: Undo a completion. Inside the ten-second window this cancels the pending write and the server is never told. Afterwards it reopens an ordinary task; a repeating task is refused, because completing it already moved it to its next occurrence.

node_id.name: Task
node_id.description: The task's id. Read it from a card, or from the node_id attribute of its button or switch.

get_nested_items.name: Get subtasks
get_nested_items.description: The children of each item in a list, keyed by the item they belong to. Use todo.get_items for the list's own items, which it returns at any size; this answers the level below that, which a to-do item has no room for.

node_id.name: List
node_id.description: The list's id. Read it from the node_id attribute of the to-do entity.

get_my_day_details.name: Get My Day details
get_my_day_details.description: For each item on My Day, the things a to-do item has no field for: its section, the path to it, its emoji and the time it is for. Use todo.get_items on the same entity for the items themselves.
